medhx: Hypertension, Hypercholesterolaemia, Benign prostatic hyperplasia, Atrial fibrillation
meds: amlodipine, valsartan, lisinopril, metoprolol, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, tamsulosin
notes: PSA 31 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.95. Prostate volume 33 mL. DRE nodus. csPCa 0.93.

note_sections.t: Persistent prostate-specific antigen elevation paired with a previously positive biopsy drives this clinical evaluation.

A seventy-seven-year-old retired bus driver presents for oncological assessment, having first undergone investigation in 2022 due to bothersome urinary symptoms that coincided with an initial PSA reading of 20.7 ng/mL and a subsequent positive biopsy. His cardiovascular profile includes hypertension, hypercholesterolaemia, and atrial fibrillation, currently stabilized on amlodipine, valsartan, lisinopril, metoprolol, simvastatin, rosuvastatin, and tamsulosin. He quit smoking in 2004 after accumulating a 12 pack-year exposure. Divorced and recently relocated, he shares a residence with his sister. Lifestyle habits include a daily forty-five-minute walking regimen with complete abstinence from alcohol. Lower urinary tract symptoms remain pronounced, registering an IPSS score of 25 out of 35, yet he denies hematuria or pelvic discomfort. A routine surveillance colonoscopy conducted by gastroenterology returned unremarkable results, and he maintains stable energy levels without meaningful weight fluctuation.

DRE — prostate: asymmetrically enlarged with a firm, discrete nodule palpable in the right posterior peripheral zone; mobility: unrestricted. General assessment reveals a blood pressure of 120/94 mmHg and a regular heart rate of 88 bpm, accompanied by clear lung fields and a soft, non-tender abdomen.

admin: Patient self-employed; flexible appointment slots requested.
